name: Street Corn Chicken Rice Bowl

ingredients.buy: 2/3 cup crumbled; 1/2 cup crumbled, for topping
juice and zest of 3 1/2 limes; 7 tablespoons
1/2 cup chopped; 2/3 cup chopped; 1 1/2 cups leaves, for topping

writer_notes: All 20 locked ingredient lines are used by a step, and no step uses anything not on the buy list. Sea Salt covers the chicken blend and the rice water; the separate Salt line covers the street corn; both are genuinely needed.
For meal prep, avocado, red onion, extra cotija, and the lime squeeze are added fresh at serving (called out in portion_html) so the avocado does not brown over the week.
Source tops with 'pickled OR fresh red onions'; the engine buys fresh Red Onion sliced, so prose commits to fresh sliced red onion only and 'pickled' is in forbidden_prose_terms.

Only locked/transcription numbers appear in prose: 7 cups corn, 4 3/4 lb chicken, 14 containers, about 20 minutes, 4 to 5 minutes per side, 165 degrees. Macros and cost are tokens ({{cal}}, {{protein}}, ${{cost_ps}}).
No per-line cost or per-ounce claims in shop_smart, since no cost_lines were provided in this dispatch to trace such a claim to.
FLAG for auditor: per-serving protein 44.6 g reads slightly high versus a rough chicken-plus-yogurt estimate (~40 g); still clears the >=40 gate. Confirm the cooked-yield/yogurt basis in the food DB.

prose.intro_html:
Mexican street corn, elote, is one of those things you eat off a stick at a summer fair and then think about for a week straight. This bowl takes that same idea, the corn folded into yogurt and lime and salty cotija, and builds a real dinner around it. Cilantro lime rice on the bottom, seasoned chicken breast on top, a generous scoop of that street corn, and avocado and red onion to finish.

The numbers do the talking here. Each container lands at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein, and the whole thing comes in at ${{cost_ps}} a serving to make. That is a lot of flavor for a dinner that keeps your protein high and your wallet shut.
prose.shop_smart:
Canned corn is the move here. The original cook used canned and drained, and you need seven cups for the full batch, so pick up enough cans to hit that and drain them well before they go in. Frozen corn works fine too, just thaw and drain it first.

Buy the chicken breast as one family pack instead of small trays, portion out the four and three quarter pounds you need, and freeze anything left over for next week. Plain Greek yogurt comes in a tub, and the spice rack does most of the heavy lifting on this one, chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and onion powder, all in teaspoon amounts.

Grab firm avocados a few days ahead so they ripen by assembly day, and treat the jalapeno as optional if your crew runs heat shy. The red onion, limes, cotija, and cilantro round out the produce and dairy run.
prose.make_it:
Start the rice. Bring the water to a boil in a large pot. Stir in the rice and the sea salt, cover, drop the heat to low, and simmer until the rice is tender, about 20 minutes. While it cooks, stir the chopped cilantro together with the fresh lime juice and lime zest in a big bowl. When the rice is done, fold it into that cilantro lime mix and set it aside.

Mix the street corn. In a large bowl, combine the drained corn, Greek yogurt, cotija, mayonnaise, lime juice and zest, the diced jalapeno if you are using it, chopped cilantro, and the salt. Stir gently until it all comes together, then taste and adjust the seasoning. Set it aside.

Season and cook the chicken. Combine the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and sea salt in a small bowl. Toss the chicken chunks in that blend until they are coated. Add the olive oil to a large skillet over medium heat, and once it is hot, cook the chicken 4 to 5 minutes per side until it is cooked through and reads 165 degrees in the middle. Work in batches so you do not crowd the pan.

Build the containers. Divide the cilantro lime rice across your 14 containers and spread it out to make room. Top each one with chicken chunks, a generous scoop of the street corn, cubed avocado, sliced red onion, a little more cilantro, and a sprinkle of crumbled cotija. A squeeze of fresh lime right before you eat brings the whole thing back to life.
prose.portion_html:
This batch fills 14 containers. Weigh the finished pot of rice, the bowl of street corn, and the cooked chicken each on their own, divide every number by 14, and that is your target scoop per container. Weighing beats eyeballing every single time, because it keeps the macros honest and stops the first few containers from getting greedy while the last few come up short.

Keep the avocado and the fresh toppings out of the containers until serving. Cube the avocado, add the red onion, sprinkle the cotija, and squeeze the lime on the day you actually eat each bowl, so the avocado does not brown and everything stays bright. The rice, corn, and chicken hold well all week.
prose.cost_closing_html:
All in, this comes out to ${{cost_ps}} per container for {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein. That is taco truck flavor for a small fraction of taco truck money, and you already made 14 of them at once.

Line it up against a fast food bowl that leaves you hungry two hours later and lighter in the wallet. This one feeds you real chicken, real corn, and real rice, and it does it on a plan you set up once and eat all week long.

In a large bowl, combine the drained corn, Greek yogurt, cotija, mayonnaise, lime juice and zest, jalapeno, cilantro, and salt, stir gently, and set aside.
Combine the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and sea salt, then toss the chicken chunks in the blend until coated.
Add the olive oil to a large skillet over medium heat and cook the chicken 4 to 5 minutes per side until it is cooked through and reads 165 degrees.
Divide the cilantro lime rice among 14 containers and top each with chicken, street corn, avocado, red onion, cilantro, cotija, and a squeeze of lime.
